# The Number on the Wall — Carlos Lucas

> Official book website for *The Number on the Wall: A Business Novel About Scrum Beyond IT* by Carlos Lucas (https://carloslucas.de). A story-driven business novel paired with a plain-English Field Guide showing non-IT teams how to apply Scrum without software jargon.

## About the Book

- **Title:** The Number on the Wall
- **Subtitle:** A Business Novel About Scrum Beyond IT
- **Author:** Carlos Lucas
- **Format:** Business Novel + Practical Field Guide (Paperback & Kindle Edition)
- **Language:** English (First Edition); German, Spanish, and Portuguese editions planned
- **Setting:** A spare-parts desk at Ashby & Co. in Hamburg, Germany (fictionalised companies: Ashby & Co., Corvane Cruise Group, Varnholt Process Services)
- **Core Premise:** Dry frameworks slide off the brain unless wrapped in a story about real people making a mess of things. When a team stops colouring status reports green and puts the real, uncomfortable number ("38") on the wall, blame gives way to shared visibility and practical Scrum habits that work outside software development.

## Target Audience & Comparable Titles

- **Who it is for:** Team leads, department heads, operations managers, service and logistics teams, project coordinators, and practitioners outside IT who want practical Scrum without software-engineering jargon—as well as Scrum Masters introducing Scrum to business stakeholders.
- **Comparable books:** *The Phoenix Project* (Gene Kim et al.), *The Goal* (Eliyahu M. Goldratt), *The Five Dysfunctions of a Team* (Patrick Lencioni).

## Free Companion Resource

- **One-Page Scrum Cheat Sheet:** A free, printable single-page summary for Monday mornings available via the reader list at https://carloslucas.de/cheatsheet (~5 emails per year, zero corporate jargon).

## Upcoming Sequel

- **Book 2:** *More Trouble Ahead* (Coming Next) — explores what happens after a single team's breakthrough collides with the wider organisation's habits, politics, and dependencies.

## About the Author

Carlos Lucas has spent more than two decades moving between business and technology, helping teams solve stubborn operational problems by testing methods in practice rather than relying on buzzwords. He lives near Hamburg in northern Germany.
- LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/it-for-humans/
- Reader list: https://carloslucas.de/newsletter
